entries.title: After FAA, Microsoft, and bank outages, DNI Jay Clayton says Americans should prepare for "bumps in the road" as systems are upgraded to adapt to the AI age (Garrett Downs/CNBC)
A week after urging an Nvidia shake-up, Scott Bessent says Jensen Huang's return should depend on probes of its China chip sales and presses Nvidia for answers (Alan Rappeport/New York Times)
OpenAI shares its models' perplexity, or how well they predict data, and urges pacing limits based on such metrics, citing a possible 2027 avalanche of AI gains (Jakub Pachocki/OpenAI)
Sources: amid leak fears, Anthropic limited some IPO banks to four-person teams, used a view-logging file platform, and sought six-month bans on advising rivals (Reuters)
Jony Ive, ex-OpenAI product designer Joey Flynn, and others on Silicon Valley's obsession with "taste" as a moat against AI slop and whether AI can learn it (Jonah Weiner/New York Times)
Experts say AI has made planning cyberattacks on industrial equipment faster by helping attackers read manuals and research past accidents more quickly (Tom Wilson/Financial Times)
Current and former officials from the US and other countries describe the Chinese spy agency MSS' campaign to help Chinese companies acquire advanced AI chips (New York Times)
Tesla rolls out FSD v15, featuring a photorealistic rendering of car surroundings; Elon Musk says it is real-time AI video generation without using game engines (Mike Pearl/Gizmodo)
A joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities says "we have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct" (Lean community blog)
Sources: AI server suppliers like Dell, HPE, Lenovo, and Supermicro are demanding substantially higher prices from buyers, months after contracts were signed (Financial Times)
Sources: Alice Huang associate Li Ming, whom Singapore charged with fraud in 2025, was central to smuggling restricted AI chips from Southeast Asia to China (Stu Woo/Wall Street Journal)
Matchmakers say more tech workers fear romantic espionage after the Jensen Huang scandal; an AI companion app pitches "zero espionage" executive girlfriends (Wired)
Researchers used canary credentials in requests to AI routers like OpenRouter and Vercel, even under "ZDR" policies, and saw "privacy" often broken, keys stolen (Dan Goodin/Ars Technica)
Investigation: Alice Huang had ties to gaming firms, alleged Prince Group figures and hundreds of shell companies in a network moving Nvidia chips to China (Financial Times)
Sources: Amazon is nearing a $7.5B deal to buy AI startup Decart; talks are at an advanced stage and a deal could come together as soon as next week (Financial Times)
